Manifest.Name: 垃圾场拾荒地图 / Dumping Ground Map
Manifest.Author: Local
Manifest.Description: 前往垃圾场时先打开地图选一块地标，确认后进入该区域，之后拾荒不再询问，本次停留内连续沿用；离开垃圾场后重新选择。地图共 5 个区域，分两档：低级区（无门槛）入口空地、生活废料带；高级区（声望解锁）拆解堆、医疗废弃点、废武器堆统一 40 点。声望按存档独立结算：每趟拾荒捡到的东西按当前金币价值累计，每 100 点价值记 1 点声望，用 ModHelper 的 mod 数据接口存进存档本体的 PlayerStore.modData（键 rep_total_value），随存档一起保存，不进 ModConfig，换存档或开新档从 0 开始；落盘时机是一天结束时的存档，中途强退当晚声望会丢，与当晚其它收益一致。未解锁的地标在地图上压暗并在编号后标出门槛，点它会提示还差多少声望。声望同时作为一行「拾荒客 / Scavenger」出现在商店评价箱（FeedbackBox）的派系声望面板里：标题后是等级名（生手 / 拾荒老手 / 熟门熟路 / 眼力毒辣 / 识货行家 / 自己人），数字是 0–200 刻度上的两位小数（`x.xx/200`，显示值 = 累计价值 / 100），绿条高度与图标解锁仍按整数点数（向下取整）沿用原生公式（65.5 × 点数 / 100），柱上有 20 / 40 / 60 / 80 / 100 五个奖励图标（未解锁半透明，但仍可悬停预览说明；20、40、80 已生效，60、100 待实现）：20 点起每天开张时多一名拾荒客客人，40 点解锁三个高级区。装了「声望增加显示 / Reputation Pop」(reputation_pop) 时，每次拾荒结算还会调用它的公开入口飘出本次 +X（用假派系 id DGM_SCAVENGER，显示「声望 · 拾荒客 / Reputation · Scavenger」，颜色用对方默认色）；对方不在时完全不解析、不装补丁、不报错。这一行只在面板打开时于内存里合成，不写存档，唯一的短路是「本次打开已建过行」（按打开序号判断，不查找子物体，避免原生 Destroy 延迟导致第二次打开被误跳过）；不对任何其它 mod 做兼容判断，其它 mod 的运行状态只写进日志。0.3.21 起在补丁关键节点输出诊断日志，前缀 [DumpingGroundMap] reputation row；0.3.25 起每趟拾荒再输出一条 [DumpingGroundMap] scavenge 日志（物品数 / 本次价值 / 累计价值 / 当前点数）。只写游戏日志、不写文件。0.3.28 起每次读档都无条件从存档重读声望并用存档值覆盖内存（不再按 runID 跳过），读回较早的自动存档后声望会回退到存档里的数值。0.3.29 起飘字改成设置里的一项（键 reputation_pop，默认开），说明文字标明依赖 Reputation Pop，未安装时本项无效、不报错。0.3.30 起设置里多一个「调试 / Debug」组：打开「启用调试项」（键 debug_enabled，默认关）后才显示并生效「设置声望点数」（键 debug_points，0–200，按 0.5 点取整），直接改写当前存档的 rep_total_value，仅供测试。0.3.31 起拾荒客声望达到 20 点后，第二天的开张流程里（前台显示之前）会在柜台上多放一枚「拾荒者信物」，每个存档只发一次，前台满则次日再试；它不影响 20 点每天多一名拾荒客客人的奖励。0.3.32 起调试项的两行都常显，不再按开关隐藏；开关即时生效，滑条 0–200、0.5 步进、松手即写入，关时仍只记一条 ignored。0.3.33 起「设置声望点数」右侧显示一位小数值，拖动时按 0.5 吸附实时更新、松手后显示真正写入的值。0.3.34 起「区域专精度」下拉框换档立即重算并刷新全部期望收益行（每区 / 各区平均 / 原版参考），不必再点「应用」；滑条拖动、预设按钮与下拉换档三条路径共用同一个刷新函数。0.3.35 起调试项修正落盘：主菜单（没有 PlayerStore）改点数时不再调用 PlayerStore.Instance（getter 会新建对象并抛 NullReferenceException），改为把点数存进游戏自己的 SaveFiles 索引，读档或新档时应用一次；已有存档时改完用原生 PlayerStore.SaveGame() 延后一帧立即落盘，不再等日终，重启后仍保留。0.3.36 起 20 点奖励的悬停说明补上「拾荒者信物」（首次达到 20 点，仅一次，放在前台）。0.3.37 起 20 点档定名「拾荒老手 / Scavenger Veteran」（名称做成常量）；首次达到 20 点除「拾荒者信物」外还在前台附一张便条（两件原子发放：便条放不下就回滚信物、不写标记、次日重来；共用同一个一次性标记）；声望 ≥20 且客人没有原生吸引原因时，拾荒客客人的来访原因显示「被「拾荒老手」的名声吸引」（UI 侧改写，不覆盖展示柜等原生原因，其它客人不受影响）。0.3.38 起客人来访原因的判据改用游戏自带的 mod 来源标记：创建这位客人时调用 ModHelper.SetClientSource 写入 sourceModId，UI 只认该标记加声望 ≥20，不再看 identifier（原生随机客池、剧情与拖车摊贩也会生成拾荒客，identifier 不唯一）；除对话记录里那行「来自 mod」外该标记不被其它系统读取，不影响议价与存档。0.3.39 起这张便条换成原生便签 handnote（小纸条面板，只有标题 / 正文 / 落款，不再是 slip 的整页文档），文案改为拾荒者第一人称「我们认你」的口吻。0.3.40 起便签文案定为：标题「写给店主 / To the shopkeeper」（标题同时是物品名），正文「这枚信物是拾荒者能力的象征。你拾荒的能力赢得了我们的尊重。往后的日子里，我们的人会常来你的店里。」，落款「拾荒者们 / — the scavengers」。0.3.41 起正文按用户原话改为「这枚信物是给有本事的人留的。你的拾荒能力赢得了我们尊重。往后的日子里，我们的人常会来店里。」，标题与落款不变。0.3.42 起正文再次按用户原话定为「这枚信物，只留给有本事的人。你的拾荒本领，我们服气。往后的日子里，我们会常来你店里照应。」。0.3.43 起英文正文换成用户选定的一句："This only goes to people who've earned it. We've seen you work the dump. We'll be by your shop from now on."，中文正文、标题与落款不变。0.3.44 起修好调试点数落盘：模组设置只能在主菜单打开，那时存档对象可能仍在内存里但 Emporium 场景已卸载，立即存档必然失败、读档又被旧值覆盖；现在只有确实在 Emporium 场景内才直接写入并立即存档，其它情况一律排队到下次读档应用，存档失败时也会自动排队兜底，并打印异常类型。0.3.45 起 40 点档定名「熟门熟路 / Knows the Back Ways」（老手是手艺，熟门熟路是门路），状态栏等级名与柱上 40 点悬停标题、说明同步换名，说明改为「凭这门路，三个高级拾荒场对你开放：拆解堆、医疗废弃点、废武器堆」。0.3.46 起声望改为五档骨架：20 拾荒老手 / 40 熟门熟路 / 60 眼力毒辣 / 80 识货行家 / 100 自己人（60 与 100 只落门槛与档名，功能待定）；80 档两项生效：高档物资出现率最低按 3% 生效（玩家设得更高时尊重设置），拆解堆 / 生活废料带 / 医疗废弃点 / 废武器堆各多出 0.5% 的满箱上锁补给箱与 0.5% 的对应钥匙卡（工程箱 + 工程卡、服务箱 + 服务卡、医疗箱 + 医疗卡、安保箱 + 安保卡；入口空地不放），两条都从普通物品份额里扣，垃圾概率不变。实现只做编译期类型绑定，不使用字符串反射或程序集扫描，清单能力保持为空。掉落由「原版表 → 本区主题表」的线性插值决定，垃圾也参与插值。垃圾 100%、专精全部时：入口 12.26、拆解 12.26、生活 12.26、医疗 14.10、废武器 14.10；默认档（垃圾 50%、专精较多）依次为 16.66 / 18.54 / 16.53 / 18.35 / 19.16，高级三区都高于低级两区。垃圾基准占比：入口 48.8%、拆解 59.9%、生活 47.7%、医疗 46.5%、废武器 51.4%。类别内物品比例回归原版，不再人工压低。设置项：垃圾出现率倍率（0–100%，默认 50%，是「该区基础垃圾率」的倍率而非垃圾占比）、高档物资出现率（0–30%，默认 0%）、区域专精度四档（较少 25% / 中等 50% / 较多 75% / 全部 100%，默认较多），以及 0.3.29 新增的「声望飘字」开关（默认开，需安装 Reputation Pop）。设置窗口先给一行固定的原版参考（垃圾 100%、无专精：五区都是 12.26），再用「原版 → 现在」列出当前设置下五区各自的结果、各区平均与三个预设；拖动实时刷新，松手或点「应用」才写盘。 / When travelling to the Dumping Ground, pick a landmark first and enter that area; later searches reuse it for the rest of the visit, and the choice resets when you leave. The map has five areas in two tiers: low tier, no requirement (Main Gate, Refuse Lane) and high tier unlocked by reputation (Scrap Pile, Medical Waste, Weapon Dump, all 40). Reputation is tracked per save: every haul adds the current cash value of what you picked up, 100 value = 1 point, stored in the save file itself through ModHelper's mod data API (PlayerStore.modData, key rep_total_value). It never goes into ModConfig, and each save or new game starts from zero. It is written when the day ends, so quitting mid-night loses that night's reputation, just like the rest of that night's gains. The mod does not read or write any files. Reputation also shows up as a "Scavenger" row in the store's feedback-box faction panel: tier name (Rookie / Scavenger Veteran / Knows the Back Ways / Keen Eye / Connoisseur / One of Us), the two-decimal point total on the native 0-200 scale (x.xx/200, total value / 100), and the bar drawn with the native formula (65.5 x floored points / 100) — icon unlocks also use floored points; five reward icons sit on the bar at 20 / 40 / 60 / 80 / 100; locked ones are translucent but still hoverable for a tooltip preview, 20, 40 and 80 are wired up while 60 and 100 are placeholders: at 20 points you get one extra scavenger customer each day when the shop opens, 40 unlocks the three gated areas, and 80 guarantees a 3% high-value floor plus a 0.5% locked supply crate and 0.5% matching keycard in Scrap Pile, Refuse Lane, Medical Waste and Weapon Dump (Main Gate keeps the vanilla table). When Reputation Pop (reputation_pop) is installed, each scavenge settlement also calls its public entry point to pop the amount gained (a synthetic faction id DGM_SCAVENGER shown as "Reputation - Scavenger" with Reputation Pop's default colour); when it is absent nothing is resolved, patched or logged as an error. The row is built in memory only when the panel opens and never touches the save; the only short-circuit is "already built for this open", tracked by an open counter rather than a child lookup (the native OpenUI destroys rows with a deferred Destroy, so a lookup would still see the previous row and skip the second open), with no compatibility branching for other mods (their run state is logged only). From 0.3.21 the patch logs diagnostic lines prefixed [DumpingGroundMap] reputation row to the game log; from 0.3.25 each haul also logs one [DumpingGroundMap] scavenge line (item count / haul value / total value / current points). It writes no files. From 0.3.28 every save load re-reads reputation from the save unconditionally (the old "same runID" skip is gone), so loading an older autosave rolls the in-memory value back to the saved one. It relies on compile-time type binding only, with no string-based reflection or assembly scanning, and the manifest declares no capabilities. From 0.3.30 a Debug group adds "Enable debug options" (debug_enabled, off by default) which reveals and enables "Set reputation points" (debug_points, 0-200, snapped to 0.5) that overwrites the current save's rep_total_value for testing. From 0.3.31, once Scavenger reputation reaches 20, the next morning's opening (before the front area is revealed) also places a Scavenger's Token on the front counter; it is granted once per save, retries the next opening if the counter is full, and does not affect the 20-point extra scavenger customer. From 0.3.32 both debug rows are always shown (no conditional hiding), the toggle takes effect immediately, and the slider (0-200, 0.5 steps) writes on release; when the toggle is off it only logs one "ignored" line. From 0.3.33 the debug slider shows its current value to the right in one decimal, updating live while dragging (snapped to 0.5) and showing the value actually written on release. From 0.3.34 changing the specialty dropdown immediately recomputes and refreshes every expected-value row (per area, average and vanilla reference) without pressing Apply; slider drags, preset buttons and the dropdown all share one refresh path. From 0.3.35 the debug setter persists immediately: changing points from the main menu (no PlayerStore loaded) no longer touches PlayerStore.Instance (whose getter would build a store and throw a NullReferenceException) but queues the value in the game's own SaveFiles index, applied once on the next load or new game; with a save loaded the native PlayerStore.SaveGame() is called one frame later so the change survives a restart instead of waiting for the end of the day. From 0.3.36 the 20-point perk tooltip lists both effects, including the one-time Scavenger's Token placed on the front counter. From 0.3.37 the 20-point perk is named Scavenger Veteran (kept as a constant); the one-time reward now also puts an accompanying note on the front counter next to the Scavenger's Token, granted atomically (if the note cannot be placed the token is rolled back, no flag is written and both are retried the next opening, sharing one one-time flag); once reputation is 20 or more, scavenger customers without a native attraction reason show "Drawn by a Scavenger Veteran's reputation" on their client card (UI-side rewrite that never overrides native reasons such as display-case attraction and leaves other customers untouched). From 0.3.38 the client-card reason test uses the game's own mod-source tag instead: the extra scavenger is tagged with this mod's id through ModHelper.SetClientSource (StoreClient.sourceModId), and the rewrite requires that tag plus 20 reputation rather than the scavenger identifier, which also comes from the random pool, story and trailer spawns. Apart from the vanilla dialog-recorder "from mod" line, nothing else reads the tag; haggling and saving are unaffected. From 0.3.39 the accompanying note uses the native handnote slip (a small panel with title / body / signature instead of the full-page slip document) and is written in the scavengers' own first-person voice ("You're one of us"). From 0.3.40 the note text is final: title "To the shopkeeper" (the title doubles as the item name), body "This token is a symbol of a scavenger's skill. Your scavenging skill has won our respect. In the days to come, our people will often come to your shop.", signature "— the scavengers". From 0.3.41 the body uses the user's exact wording: "This token is left for people with skill. Your scavenging skill has won our respect. In the days to come, our people will often come to the shop." From 0.3.42 the body is "This token is only left for people with skill. Your scavenging skill — we're convinced. In the days to come, we'll often come by your shop to look after you." From 0.3.43 the English body is "This only goes to people who've earned it. We've seen you work the dump. We'll be by your shop from now on." (Chinese body, title and signature unchanged). From 0.3.44 the debug setter persists correctly: the settings window only opens from the main menu, where the store object can still exist while the Emporium scene is gone, so the immediate save always failed and the next load restored the old value; it now writes and saves directly only inside the Emporium scene and otherwise queues the value for the next load, with an automatic queue fallback when a save fails and the exception type logged. From 0.3.45 the 40-point tier is named "Knows the Back Ways" (the veteran has the skill, this one has the connections); the tier name, the 40-point hover title and its description are updated together, with the description reading "With the back ways known, three high-tier scavenging grounds open up to you: Scrap Pile, Medical Waste, Weapon Dump". From 0.3.46 reputation has a five-tier skeleton (20 Scavenger Veteran / 40 Knows the Back Ways / 60 Keen Eye / 80 Connoisseur / 100 One of Us; 60 and 100 only carry the threshold and name for now). The 80-point tier guarantees the high-value slider works at 3% or higher (higher player settings are kept) and adds a 0.5% full locked supply crate and a 0.5% matching keycard to Scrap Pile, Refuse Lane, Medical Waste and Weapon Dump (engineering / service / medical / security pairs; Main Gate gets nothing). Both shares come out of normal items, so junk chance is unchanged. Locked landmarks are dimmed, carry their requirement next to the number, and explain the shortfall when clicked. Loot is a linear blend between the vanilla table and the area's themed table, junk included. At 100% junk and full specialty: Main Gate 12.26, Scrap Pile 12.26, Refuse Lane 12.26, Medical Waste 14.10, Weapon Dump 14.10. At the default (50% junk, High specialty): 16.66 / 18.54 / 16.53 / 18.35 / 19.16, so all three gated areas beat both low-tier ones. Base junk shares: 48.8% / 59.9% / 47.7% / 46.5% / 51.4%. Within-category ratios follow vanilla again, with no manual suppression. Settings: a junk chance multiplier (0-100%, default 50% - a multiplier on each area's base junk chance, not a junk share), a high-value chance slider (0-30%, default 0%) and a four-tier specialty dropdown (Rare 25% / Medium 50% / High 75% / All 100%, default High), plus a 0.3.29 "Reputation pop-ups" toggle (on by default, requires Reputation Pop). The settings window first shows a fixed vanilla reference (100% junk, no specialty: 12.26 everywhere), then "vanilla -> now" for each area at the current settings, the average and three presets. Everything refreshes while dragging; the config is written on release or when Apply is pressed.
